slides.title: Ship it, **or stop?**
slides.sub: Production throws one error. Your laptop throws a different one.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout stands on a ship's deck gripping a big ship's wheel, hesitating, with a large round red button beside him; on the left a server rack belches a little puff of smoke, on the right a laptop shows a different small glitch spark. Corey's face is torn between excitement and doubt, a seagull watching him sceptically from the railing.

slides.label: What most of us do
slides.caption: A nearby error feels like confirmation. So we ship.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout, wide-eyed with excitement, slams a big red launch button with both leaf-arms while a small rocket blasts off behind him trailing sparkles, the launch pad still visibly held together with sticky tape.

slides.caption: I shipped. Wrong twice over. It looked done for about a day.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout celebrates in front of a wall of glowing green status lights with confetti and a party hat, arms raised in triumph, completely unaware that behind the wall a growing plume of smoke and a small fire are starting to spread, and a fire extinguisher sits forgotten in the corner.
slides.label: What I did
The rule I keep now
slides.caption: The gap between the two errors is the finding. **Stop there.**
slides.scene: Corey the sprout stands calmly in the middle of a busy road holding up a big round stop paddle like a lollipop lady, while a line of tiny cartoon delivery vans marked only with abstract shapes screech to a halt in front of him, drivers looking surprised.

slides.text: What's the most confident wrong fix you've ever shipped?
